A window into life in Chammanur, Punnayoorkulam

Stories from the heart of Chammanur.

Chammanur is a small village in Punnayoorkulam, on the coast of Thrissur district — known for its paddy fields, its temple festivals, and the people who have called it home for generations. This is where we keep its stories, its voices, and its everyday life.

Most families here have farmed or fished this land for generations, though many young people now work in Kochi, Bangalore, or the Gulf. This site exists to keep the village connected — its stories, its elders' memories, its festivals, and the everyday moments that don't usually get written down. Share a story if you have one to tell.

Stories of Chammanur

Voices · Memories · Poems
Memory 2026

When the Pooram began at dawn

By Raman Nair·Chammanur

I still remember the sound of the chenda before I could see the procession. In those days, the whole village seemed to wake up together. People came walking from every direction, carrying little lamps and talking about the day's celebrations...

The old tank was where everyone gathered. Children stood on the edges trying to see above the crowd, while the older men found their familiar places beneath the trees.

There were fewer vehicles, fewer loudspeakers and, perhaps, fewer distractions. But somehow the morning felt bigger.

Even now, when I hear the first chenda from a distance, I am taken back to those mornings. The village has changed, but that sound has not.

Village Story 2026

The last paddy field near our house

By Leela Krishnan·Chammanur

There used to be water everywhere after the first rain. My mother knew exactly when the field would be ready, and my father could tell from the colour of the soil whether the season would be good.

Today, most of that field has become houses. We still have one small patch behind our home, and every year we try to cultivate it.

It is not much, but when the green shoots appear, the place feels like the Chammanur I remember.

Poem 2026

My village after rain

By Anitha Menon·Chammanur

After the rain,
the canal remembers the sky.
Coconut leaves whisper
above the quiet road.

Somewhere a bicycle passes,
a kettle begins to sing,
and the village slowly opens
its wet green eyes.

Memory 2025

The school under the tiled roof

By Joseph Mathew·Chammanur

Our classroom had two windows, three long benches and a blackboard that was never completely black. We complained about the heat then. Now, strangely, I miss it.

Every generation seems to leave something behind in that old building. Names scratched into desks, photographs on the walls, and memories that return whenever former students meet.

What our elders say

Oral history
"
In our time there was no electricity till late in the evening. We studied by the light of a kerosene lamp, and still no one in our house failed an exam.
Kunjukrishnan Nair, 82 — farmer, Chammanur
"
The pond near the temple never dried up, even in the worst summers. My grandmother used to say the land itself was blessed by the goddess.
Devaki Amma, 76 — homemaker, Punnayoorkulam
"
We walked four miles to the nearest school. Nobody complained — that was simply how it was done, and we were glad to be going at all.
Raghavan Master, 79 — retired schoolteacher
